note: Provisional thresholds. Frozen before any BARC label was joined to rulebook output. Not tuned on BARC. Any later tuning must use a new version string and a separate results folder.

field._doc: Interior = parcel buffered inward in the tile's UTM CRS (metric). Spectral checks use the native 20 m grid: 20 m bands read natively, 10 m bands 2x2-mean aggregated, so no band is upsampled and one acquisition = one observation.

season._doc: MM-DD within the crop year. The corn cycle is the summer peak; a spring peak before a spring minimum is recorded as preceding green cover, not the corn season.

identity._doc: Assumption: a field-mean summer NDVI peak >= 0.70 is consistent with a closed corn canopy; 0.55-0.70 = uncertain identity (review); < 0.55 = not a corn-like cycle. Sweet corn / popcorn / non-corn can only be excluded from records; none exist for this dataset, so that check is not_applicable.

quality._doc: Clear look = >= 60 % of interior 20 m pixels SCL 4/5 and >= 3 valid pixels (extraction rule, 02b_extract_s2_20m.py).

radar_orbit._doc: Per crop year and area: choose the single relative orbit that fully covers (median S1 pixel count >= 90 % of the 10 m interior pixel count) the most fields, then the most Jul-Dec dates. Not merely the most frequent orbit. Fields not fully covered by that orbit get radar = unknown (geometry).

removal._doc: Candidate optical change = consecutive clear looks a -> b after the summer peak with NDVI(a) - NDVI(b) >= 0.15 and NDVI(b) <= 0.40. It is accepted as canopy REMOVAL on optical evidence only if (i) the drop exceeds what senescence could produce over the gap, i.e. drop >= 0.012/day x (b - a) + 0.10 (ASSUMPTION A3: natural senescence lowers field-mean NDVI by at most ~0.012/day), and (ii) a later clear look within 30 d stays <= NDVI(b) + 0.10. A candidate failing (i) or (ii) needs an overlapping radar structural change; otherwise it is senescence/decline only. A return to >= NDVI(a) - 0.10 within 30 d = ambiguous removal vs damage (review). Radar-only removal (no optical candidate) requires non-green canopy (NDVI <= 0.50) at the last optical look before the radar interval and no green look after it. An NDVI threshold crossing alone never establishes harvest. v1.1: candidate pairs are any two clear looks <= max_window_days apart (plus consecutive looks at any gap); processed in order of first-removed date, narrowest interval first. NOT YET HARVESTED requires no post-peak look <= senescence_ndvi (a post-decline green-up is flagged as a possible cover crop, not standing corn).

condition._doc: Evaluated at the last standing look a. Its age relative to harvest is at most b - a; if b - a > 15 d the condition is UNCERTAIN (too distant). Dry-down start = first look after the peak with NDVI <= peak - 0.10 after which no look before a exceeds peak - 0.05; duration = a - start (lower bound, uses a, not b). GREEN = NDVI green AND NDRE green AND no >= 25 d dry-down. DRY = NDVI dry AND (NDRE senescent OR dry-down >= 25 d) AND NDRE not green.

timing.gdd_method: daily (min(Tmax,86F) + max(Tmin,50F))/2 - 50F, Tmax/Tmin clipped to [50,86] F
timing.weather_source: Open-Meteo historical weather API (ERA5-based reanalysis), daily 2 m Tmax/Tmin (F) and precipitation (mm), one point at the mean field centroid

sources.ref: Miller, J. (March 2025) Corn Growth Stages and Management. University of Delaware Cooperative Extension fact sheet, Table 1 (GDD, 86/50 F): R5 2287 (range 2029-2509), R6 2824 (range 2686-2926), VE 109 (84-150).

Timing Corn Silage Harvest. University of Wisconsin Corn Agronomy (2014, updated 2016): silage harvest usually begins around 50 % kernel milk, 42-47 days after silking; ~55-60 days from silking to R6 black layer.

Leaf collar emergence about every 82 GDD (Nielsen, Purdue) to 84 GDD (Abendroth et al. 2011, Iowa State PMR 1009) from VE to V10; emergence ~115-120 GDD after planting. Summarised in OSU Agronomic Crops Network 'Predicting leaf development in corn using accumulated heat units'.

timing._doc: Planting is unknown, so it is bounded from the satellite canopy-detection date D (first look after the spring minimum with NDVI >= 0.35). ASSUMPTION A1 (not from a source): field-mean NDVI first reaches 0.35 between V4 and V8, i.e. 120 + 4x84 ~ 450 to 120 + 8x84 ~ 800 GDD after planting. Planting interval = dates where GDD(P -> D) in [450, 800]. GDD at harvest: min = GDD(latest planting -> a), max = GDD(earliest planting -> b). SILAGE TIMING if max < 2686 (before the earliest regional black layer) and min >= 2029 (at/after the earliest regional dent). GRAIN TIMING if min >= 2926 (past the latest regional black layer) and the canopy dried while standing. Otherwise TIMING UNKNOWN; hybrid relative maturity is unknown and the regional ranges stand in for it. Removal with max < 2029 = exception flag (earlier than any silage stage).

surface._doc: ASSUMPTION A2 (no validated published NDTI cut-off was found): first clear look after removal (within 20 d) with NDVI <= 0.30; NDTI <= 0.05 = little residue (silage support), NDTI >= 0.10 = abundant residue (grain support), between = unknown. NDTI is a proxy for residue, not a measurement. Moisture strongly affects SWIR indices, so >= 10 mm rain in the 2 days before the look = SURFACE UNKNOWN. Absence of rain does not establish dry soil (irrigation unknown). Manure, tillage and residue removal cannot be identified and are listed as confounders.

radar._doc: Structural change at S1 date t: mean over acquisitions in (t-24 d, t] minus mean over [t-24 d-, t) with >= 2 each side: dVH <= -1.5 dB AND d(VH-VV) <= -0.5 dB (cross-ratio falls when canopy volume scattering is removed). dVV >= +1.0 dB = wetting signature -> RADAR UNKNOWN. Change interval = [last acquisition before t, t]. Corroborates optical removal if intervals overlap within 6 d. If |dVH| < 0.5 dB across the optical interval (>= 2 acquisitions each side) radar contradicts removal. GRAIN SUPPORT if the radar change starts >= 25 d after optical senescence onset (first NDVI <= 0.50 after peak). Magnitude alone never classifies.

exceptions._doc: Possible confounders are flagged, never asserted: frost (Tmin <= 28.4 F = -2 C) while the canopy was still green before removal; Jun-Aug precipitation < 150 mm (possible drought stress). Lodging, disease, earlage / high-moisture grain and partial harvest by product cannot be observed; listed as unverifiable confounders. Zone check: 2x2 zone NDVI removal intervals that do not overlap within 10 d = possible mixed management (review, no homogeneous label).

excluded_sources: BARC Corn 2021-2023.gpkg and any copy or derivative
any publication or report disclosing BARC silage/grain field labels
documents._doc: Direct-evidence checks (step 3) and contextual checks (step 11) read only a curated registry of verifiable items (URL, excerpt/location, field match, crop year, planned vs actual, retrieval date). v1 registry is empty: no field-linked public harvest, delivery, nutrient-management or dairy records were identified that are not excluded. Absence is recorded as unknown, never as evidence.

changelog.outputs: label-free run kept in results_v1/run_v1.0_prelabel/ (44 field-years: 9 NOT YET HARVESTED, 3 LIKELY GRAIN, 32 UNRESOLVED)

changelog.why: Defects found by inspecting v1.0 traces and input series WITHOUT reference labels: (1) 2022 legacy-collection reflectance was double-offset (NDVI up to 8.7) -> fixed at extraction, not in the rules; (2) post-harvest cover-crop green-up (NDVI back to ~0.5 in Nov-Dec after falling to ~0.25) was read as standing corn -> NOT YET HARVESTED now requires that the canopy never fell to the senescence level after the peak; (3) with 2-5 day revisits a harvest appears as a fall spread over several consecutive looks, which a consecutive-pair detector cannot see -> candidates now include any two looks <= 15 d apart (still required to fall faster than senescence); (4) the radar-only 'no green look afterwards' test now covers only the 30-day confirmation window so later cover crops do not veto it.
changelog.thresholds_changed: none (one new structural setting: removal.max_window_days = 15, equal to condition.max_preharvest_obs_age_days)
